**So the correct sentence is-** *I'm certainly going to start studying from today. *

questions.question:
**Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select ‘No substitution required’.**

There were a dozen eggs in the basket, but now __there will be__ only six.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is** 'there are'**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• According to the given sentence, the first says that 'there were a dozen eggs in the basket' that means 'previously it was only a dozen eggs' and the second conveys that 'now there are only six'
 
• 'Now' is an adverb that conveys the present time. (at the present time, not in the past or future)
 
 
• Example- She used to be a teacher, but **now she works in publishing.**
 
 
 
• Hence, in the given sentence, we need to use a present tense so the correct part will be 'there are'

**So the correct sentence is-** *There were a dozen eggs in the basket, but now **there are** only six. *

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/51867102c7c2f369f6e29d2efe025e3b3367c68261ec20262828d84ca5c8f854.png] **Hinglish__**

__
 
• दिए गए वाक्य के अनुसार, पहला कहता है कि 'टोकरी में एक दर्जन अंडे थे' जिसका अर्थ है 'पहले यह केवल एक दर्जन अंडे थे' और दूसरा बताता है कि 'अब केवल छह हैं'
 
• 'अभी' (now) एक क्रिया विशेषण है जो वर्तमान समय का बोध कराता है। (वर्तमान समय में, भूत या भविष्य में नहीं)
 
 
• उदाहरण- She used to be a teacher, but now she works in publishing.
 
 
 
• इसलिए, दिए गए वाक्य में, हमें वर्तमान काल का उपयोग करने की आवश्यकता है, इसलिए सही भाग 'वहाँ हैं' (there are) होगा।

तो सही वाक्य है- *There were a dozen eggs in the basket, but now **there are** only six. *

questions.question:
**Identify the segment in the sentence which contains a grammatical error.**

Vijaya saw the play in a auditorium near her house.
questions.solution:
The erroneous part is **'in a auditorium'**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In the given part, the usage of 'a' is incorrect instead of it we have to use '**an**'.
 
• In the given sentence, 'auditorium' is a countable noun that means 'a theatre or concert hall where the audience sits.'
 
• The word is pronounced with a vowel sound hence, we need to use 'an' instead of 'a'. The indefinite article 'an' is used with singular, countable nouns that are preceded by a vowel sound.
 
 
• Example- Johnny Depp is **an actor.**
 
 

**So the correct sentence is-** *Vijaya saw the play in **an auditorium** near her house.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/51867102c7c2f369f6e29d2efe025e3b3367c68261ec20262828d84ca5c8f854.png] **Hinglish__**

questions.question: 84 persons take 56 days to complete a certain task. When one-fourth of the task was completed, one-seventh of the workers left. How many days in all does it take to complete the entire task?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Days taken for **one-fourth** of the task = 56 ÷ 4 = 14 days.

Remaining workers = 84 − (1/7 × 84) = 72 persons.

Remaining work ratio = 3/4.

Days for remaining task = (Original Workers × Remaining original days) ÷ Remaining Workers

Days for remaining task = (84 × 42) ÷ 72 = 49 days.

Total time = 14 + 49 = 63 days.

**∴ The correct answer is 63 days.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Total workers = 84 persons

Initial time to complete task = 56 days

Work completed = 1/4 of the task

Workers leaving = 1/7 of the total strength

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/acd3e027abf9aca87c529016fe6d62df364d0bdd7ba20eb9265c90ea2f43ac80.png] 

**Step-by-step Calculation:**

⇒ Total work in man-days = 84 × 56 units

⇒ Time taken to complete 1/4 task = (1/4) × 56 = 14 days

⇒ Remaining work = 1 − 1/4 = 3/4 of total work

⇒ Remaining work in units = (3/4) × 84 × 56 = 84 × 42 units

⇒ Number of workers left = (1/7) × 84 = 12 persons

⇒ Remaining workers = 84 − 12 = 72 persons

⇒ Days for remaining work = (Remaining Work Units) ÷ (Remaining Workers)

⇒ Days for remaining work = (84 × 42) ÷ 72

⇒ Days for remaining work = (7 × 42) ÷ 6 = 7 × 7 = 49 days

⇒ Total days = Days for 1/4 task + Days for 3/4 task

⇒ Total days = 14 + 49 = 63 days

**∴ The correct answer is 63 days.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Chain Rule Formula

The relationship between work, men, and days is given by (M₁ × D₁) / W₁ = (M₂ × D₂) / W₂, where M is persons, D is days, and W is work.

Inverse Proportion

For a constant amount of work, the number of persons is inversely proportional to the time taken (M₁D₁ = M₂D₂).

Man-Day Concept

Total work is often measured in man-days, which is the product of the number of men and the number of days they work.</p

questions.question: The amount obtained by investing a certain sum at r% p.a. for 3 years at simple interest is equal to the simple interest on the same sum at the same rate for 13 years. The value of r is:
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Amount (3 years) = Simple Interest (13 years)

Principal + SI (3 years) = SI (13 years)

Principal = SI (13 years) − SI (3 years) = SI (10 years)

For Principal (100%) to be equal to 10 years of interest, the annual rate must be 100% ÷ 10 = 10%.

**∴ The correct answer is 10%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

Given: Principal = P, Rate = r% p.a., Time₁ = 3 years, Time₂ = 13 years.

Formula: Simple Interest (SI) = (P × r × t) / 100 | Amount (A) = P + SI.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e552677647a3c1a5a8ccc89628e0ec8f32a92be16f78caf004cf79d8fcf6f1a6.png] 

⇒ Amount after 3 years = P + (P × r × 3) / 100

⇒ Simple Interest for 13 years = (P × r × 13) / 100

⇒ According to the question: P + 3Pr/100 = 13Pr/100

⇒ P = 13Pr/100 − 3Pr/100

⇒ P = 10Pr/100

⇒ 1 = 10r/100

⇒ 1 = r/10

⇒ r = 10

**∴ The correct answer is 10%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Simple Interest Basics

Simple Interest is calculated only on the principal amount. The formula is SI = P × R × T / 100, where P is Principal, R is Rate, and T is Time.

Amount in Simple Interest

The total amount (A) at the end of the period is the sum of the principal and interest: A = P + SI = P(1 + RT/100).

Effective Rate of Interest

The effective interest earned over T years is (R × T)% of the principal. In this problem, the difference in time (13 − 3 = 10 years) represents the principal itself.</p

questions.question: A sum of Rs. 3,780 is divided between A, B and C such that if their shares are decreased by Rs. 130, Rs. 150 and Rs. 200, respectively, then they are in the ratio of 5 : 2 : 4. What is the original share of C?
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Total reduction in the shares of **A, B and C** = 130 + 150 + 200 = **Rs. 480**.

Remaining sum to be divided = 3,780 − 480 = **Rs. 3,300**.

Total ratio parts = 5 + 2 + 4 = **11 units**.

11 units = 3,300 ⇒ 1 unit = 300.

**C's original share** = (4 units × 300) + 200 = 1,200 + 200 = **Rs. 1,400**.

**∴ The correct answer is Rs. 1,400.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Total sum = **Rs. 3,780**

Decreases in shares = **Rs. 130**, **Rs. 150**, and **Rs. 200**

New ratio = **5 : 2 : 4**

**Formula Used:**

Total Sum = (Sum of Decreased Shares) + (Sum of Reductions)

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/9ea1b79935bd4ead74b2a51a9172d85daebe17fbbb492b5387d5d5fc586248b2.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Total decrease = 130 + 150 + 200 = **Rs. 480**

⇒ Total share in ratio = 3,780 − 480 = **Rs. 3,300**

⇒ Sum of ratios = 5 + 2 + 4 = **11 units**

⇒ 11 units = 3,300

⇒ 1 unit = 3,300 ÷ 11 = **Rs. 300**

⇒ C's decreased share = 4 × 300 = **Rs. 1,200**

⇒ C's original share = 1,200 + 200 = **Rs. 1,400**

**∴ The correct answer is Rs. 1,400.**

**__Additional Information__**

Ratio Division

To divide a quantity **S** into the ratio **a : b : c**, the shares are calculated as (a/k)×S, (b/k)×S, and (c/k)×S, where k = a + b + c.

Net Amount Calculation

When individual shares are decreased by specific constants, the total sum of the system decreases by the **sum of those constants**.

Inverse Variation in Ratios

If **x** is inversely proportional to **y**, then the ratio of x₁ : x₂ is equal to the inverse ratio y₂ : y₁.</p

questions.question: A shopkeeper marks an article 24% above its cost price and allows a 15% discount on the marked price. If he earns a profit of Rs. 27 by selling the article, then the selling price of the article is:

Market Price = cost price + 24% of cost price

Discount = 15%

**Formula used**

Selling price = Market Price - Discount

Profit = Selling price - Cost Price

when Selling price > Cost price

**Calculation**

Let the cost price is Rs.x

Market price = x + 24% of x

⇒ 124x/100

Discount = 15% of (124x/100)

⇒ 1860x/10000

Selling price = (124x/100) - (1860x/10000)

⇒ (12400x - 1860x)/10000

⇒ 10540x/10000

Profit = selling price - cost price

27 = (10540x/10000) - x

⇒ 27 = (10540x - 10000x)/10000

⇒ 27 = 540x/10000

x = (27 × 10000)/540

x = 500

Selling price = 500 + 27

⇒ Rs. 527

questions.question: What does Article 360 of the Constitution of India provide with?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **__Financial emergency.__**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Article 360 of the Constitution of India empowers the president to proclaim a financial emergency on the following ground**:

 
 
• If the president is satisfied that a situation has arisen due to which the financial stability or credibility of India is threatened or in danger.
 
• The** 38th Constitutional Amendment Act 1975** made the satisfaction of the president in declaring a financial emergency final and conclusive.
 
• The satisfaction of the president is held up in any court on any ground. However 44th Constitutional Amendment Act 1978 deleted this provision.
 
• This means the satisfaction of the president is under Judicial review.
 
• The President may issue directions for the reduction of salaries and allowances to the judges of the Supreme Court and the High Courts and of all or any class of persons serving the Union.
 
• Till now, the Financial Emergency has never been invoked in India.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Article 21:**

 
 
• It lays down that, “No person shall be deprived of his life or personal liberty except according to a procedure established by law".
 
• It assures every person the right to life and personal liberty.
 
 
 
• **Fundamental duties:**
 
 
• In the Constitution of India, fundamental duties are mentioned in article 51A.
 
• There was no list of fundamental duties in the original constitution.
 
• Fundamental duties were added into the Indian constitution by the 42nd constitutional amendment act 1976.
 
• the 42nd constitutional amendment added part IV A and Article 51A to the Indian constitution.
 
• Fundamental duties were added into the Indian constitution on the recommendation of the Swaran Singh Committee.
 
• Initially, there were only 10 fundamental duties in the constitution.
 
• The 86th constitutional amendment act 2002 added one more fundamental duty to the constitution.
 
• Currently, there are 11 fundamental duties in the Indian constitution.
 
• The idea of fundamental duties was borrowed from the Russian constitution.
 
• Fundamental duties are non-justiciable in nature.
 
 
 
• **The right to property:**
 
 
• It was deleted from the list of Fundamental Rights by the 44th Amendment Act, 1978.
 
• It is made a legal right under Article 300-A in Part XII of the Constitution. So at present, there are only six Fundamental Rights.
 
• Article 19 provided to all citizens the right to acquire, hold, and dispose of the property whereas Article 31 provides that "no person shall be deprived of his property save by authority of law."
 
• Later, in 44th Amendment of 1978 deleted the right to property from the list of fundamental rights.
 
• Hence, the right to property is no longer a fundamental right, however, it is still a constitutional right.

questions.question: The difference between Revenue Receipts plus Non-debt Capital Receipts (NDCR) and total expenditure is called ______.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **__Fiscal Deficit.__**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The difference between Revenue Receipts plus Non-debt Capital Receipts (NDCR) and total expenditure is called **Fiscal Deficit.__**
 
• It occurs when the government's expenditure exceeds its income.
 
• This difference is calculated both in absolute terms and also as a percentage of the Gross Domestic Product (GDP) of the country.
 
• A recurring high fiscal deficit means that the government has been spending beyond its means.
 
• Similarly, the government describes the fiscal deficit of India as “the excess of total disbursements from the Consolidated Fund of India, excluding repayment of the debt, over total receipts into the Fund (excluding the debt receipts) during a financial year".
 
• **Fiscal Deficit = Total expenditure of the government (capital and revenue expenditure) - Total income of the government (Revenue receipts + recovery of loans + other receipts).**
 
• A high fiscal deficit is not always bad, it can also be good for the economy if the money spent goes into the creation of productive assets like highways, roads, ports, and airports that boost economic growth and result in job creation.
 
• The government meets the fiscal deficit by borrowing money. In a way, the total borrowing requirements of the government in a financial year are equal to the fiscal deficit in that year.
 
• If interest payments are included in the** primary deficit,** it is equal to the fiscal deficit.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

 
• **Revenue deficit:**

 
 
• It arises when the government's revenue expenditure exceeds the total revenue receipts.
 
• This deficit includes those transactions that have a direct impact on a government's current income and expenditure.
 
• The deficit represents that the government's own earnings are not sufficient to meet the day-to-day operations of its departments.
 
 
 
• **Effective Revenue Deficit:**
 
 
• Effective Revenue Deficit = Revenue Deficit - Grants in aid for the creation of capital assets.
